graph.title: Make It Rain Clap Machine (Arduino MKR Zero)

new_part_types.name: Laser-cut MDF box (base, lid, motor holders)

notes: The manual's circuit diagram and schematic were not readable in the supplied images, so the wiring is reconstructed from the text: I2S mic SD->A6, SCK->D2, FS/WS->D3; DC motor driven by an N-MOSFET with a flyback diode, a 2.2k pull-down on the gate, and a 0.1uF and a 100uF capacitor across the motor; servo signal level-shifted to 5V with an N-MOSFET and a 2.2k pull-up.
The MKR Zero pins for the DC-motor gate (D6) and servo signal (D7) are assumed. The manual does not name them.
The microphone is placed on the breadboard in columns 1-6 with VDD on 3.3V (VCC), GND and LR to ground. The ICS43432 breakout pin order is assumed.
The MKR Zero, microphone, rubber band and the MDF pieces are not in the supplied catalogue, so they are new part types. The MDF wheel, lifting arm and box are simplified single parts.
The servo's 3-pin connector is modelled as direct leads into the breadboard. Its V+ and GND go into the 5V and GND rails.
The breadboard hole and rail positions are chosen for a plausible layout. Rail positions are arbitrary.
Jumper wires to the MKR Zero are modelled as plain jumper-wire attached to header-pin ports. Colours are guesses.
Both capacitors use the catalogue 'capacitor' type, with the value prop distinguishing 0.1uF from 100uF. The electrolytic's polarity is not modelled.
The 100uF capacitor's polarity is not captured. A second 3.3V gate tie for the servo MOSFET is wired to the 3V3 rail (tp.4).

breadboard.name: Solderless breadboard
breadboard.port_rule: Holes are named '<column><bank>.<row>': column 1-30, bank 't' (top half, rows a-e) or 'b' (bottom half, rows f-j), e.g. '12t.c', '7b.h'. The 5 holes of one column-bank are one strip. Power rails: 'tp.<n>', 'tn.<n>', 'bp.<n>', 'bn.<n>' (each rail is one strip).
